G-F091.trick: SAME DAVE: Sensory = Afferent (Arrives), Motor = Efferent (Exits).
G-F091.tip: Direction is about the CNS: toward it = afferent, away from it = efferent. Ignore how the drawing is laid out.

G-F092.trick: NISSL bodies = rough ER "nibbles" in the cell body making proteins.
G-F092.tip: Nissl substance is rough ER found in the soma and dendrites, never in the axon.

G-F093.trick: Schwann = Single segment, PNS. Oligodendrocyte = One cell, many CNS axons (oligo = few branches).
G-F093.tip: Myelin maker: Schwann cells in the PNS, oligodendrocytes in the CNS.

G-F094.trick: EPENDYMAL cells = the lining of the brain's fluid caves (ventricles), with cilia to stir CSF.
G-F094.tip: CNS glia: astrocytes (support, blood–brain barrier), microglia (immune), oligodendrocytes (myelin), ependymal (line ventricles, CSF).

G-F095.trick: HYPER-polarized = extra negative = farther from the firing line.
G-F095.tip: More negative than rest = hyperpolarization = less likely to fire. Toward zero = depolarization = more likely.

G-F096.trick: Na+/K+ pump: "3 Salty Out, 2 Potassium In" (3 Na+ out, 2 K+ in).
G-F096.tip: Remember the ratio 3:2 and the directions: sodium leaves, potassium enters, one ATP per cycle.

G-F097.trick: Action potentials are like a light switch, not a dimmer: all-or-none. Stronger stimulus = flicks faster.
G-F097.tip: A stronger stimulus raises the firing frequency, not the size of each spike.

G-F098.trick: Sodium rushes IN to rise; Potassium POURS out to fall.
G-F098.tip: Depolarization = Na+ in. Repolarization = K+ out. Overshoot past rest = hyperpolarization.

G-F099.trick: Block reuptake = leave the music on longer: the transmitter stays in the cleft.
G-F099.tip: This is how SSRIs work: blocking reuptake keeps serotonin acting longer.

G-F100.trick: CONvergence = many roads COming together into one town.
G-F100.tip: Convergence = many → one. Divergence = one → many.

C-ch10-divisions.trick: CNS = the Central command (brain + cord). PNS = the Phone lines out to the body.
C-ch10-divisions.tip: Brain and spinal cord only = CNS. Nerves and ganglia outside them = PNS.

C-ch10-neurons.trick: Neuron = the body's messenger wire: dendrites listen, axon talks.
C-ch10-neurons.tip: Neurons send signals; glial cells support them. Mature neurons rarely divide.

C-ch10-glia.trick: Myelin = insulation tape on a wire that lets the signal jump node to node (saltatory = leaping).
C-ch10-glia.tip: Myelin makes white matter white and speeds conduction. Loss of myelin (as in MS) slows signals.

C-ch10-resting.trick: RMP ≈ −70 mV: the inside of a resting neuron is negative, like a charged battery.
C-ch10-resting.tip: Resting potential is kept by the Na+/K+ pump and K+ leak channels.

C-ch10-impulse.trick: Threshold ≈ −55 mV: the point of no return, like a toilet that flushes once you push past the click.
C-ch10-impulse.tip: Reach threshold and a full action potential fires. Below threshold, nothing fires.

C-ch10-synapses.trick: SYN-apse = where two cells "clasp" (synapse = junction) without touching.
C-ch10-synapses.tip: Chemical synapse order: impulse arrives → Ca2+ enters → vesicles release transmitter → receptors respond.
